rows.strategy: Large window, exact cache on
rows.note: First seed: the model filtered batches with code and about 91% of prompt tokens were cached. Second seed: no answers. It let every batch into its context and re-typed it, grew about 13K tokens per batch, and the server refused the next request at about 246K, one batch before the questions arrived. Its running table was exact up to that point; it had never been told its window size. A third try with the window shown and a fetch guard also returned nothing: the model re-types every batch and thinks at length, and no guard changes that.

An earlier seed-1 attempt also returned 18/18 but was void because it wrote unasked values to the answer file; that invalid attempt is not the result shown here.

rows.strategy: Keep everything in the window, narrative text

rows.strategy: No management, files allowed, narrative text
rows.note: Same narrative task. The model saved the batches to files, wrote a script that pulls out the sentences naming a counter, and read only those. Search narrowed the reading; nothing was lost because the text stayed on disk.

rows.strategy: Read-mode self-editing agent, narrative text, 480K stream (larger than the window)

rows.strategy: Table plus archive and recall, narrative text with questions about dropped text

Dropped batches go verbatim to an archive the model can only read, with a search tool. Every answer right, including the twelve about dropped text; it searched the archive 12 times. Nothing is deleted, only moved out of view.

disk_estimate.status: Calculated payload and illustrative transfers; no completed disk-cache benchmark
disk_estimate.attention_payload_formula: 16 layers * 2 arrays * 4 KV heads * 256 head dimension * 2 bytes; target attention KV only, summed across both GPUs
disk_estimate.assumptions: One complete read of the attention cache at the stated hypothetical sustained storage bandwidth. Not an output-token rate. Excludes computation, recurrent/draft state, padding, metadata, and additional unoverlapped transfer. Partial residence, pipelining and speculative acceptance change the model calculation.
disk_estimate.streaming_status: Not implemented or benchmarked in the cited experiments

timing_analysis.method: Wall time and tool time from saved run records. Reading estimated from cold-read rates; writing is a residual and includes call overhead. Summary-call times are estimated. No per-token timestamps or isolated disk-I/O measurements.

cache_reuse.method: Common prefixes measured in rendered characters and converted to tokens with per-call ratios; not exact tokenization.

cache_break_even.method: Counterfactual calculation from saved calls and measured/assumed cold-read rates; not a paired cache-off run.

edit_cost.about: Wait before the first output token after one edit (a deletion) inside a cached prompt, exact prefix cache on. first_edit_s: first request after the edit; repeat_s: the same edited prompt sent again; cold_s: the same prompt with nothing cached. Fill a cell by setting status to "measured" and the three times, then run scripts/organize_results.py and scripts/build_site.py.

distance_probes.question: An agent works on one task whose history is many times larger than its live window. Questions planted at known distances back (counted in batches, called items in the evidence files) show what each way of managing the window still remembers, and whether it still follows a rule and a method stated at the start. The keeper section asks whether something outside the agent can do that managing.
distance_probes.task: Sparse prose stream: about 240K tokens (240,208 on seed 0, in 147 batches), about 3 counter changes per batch. Every 25 batches a probe asks three questions about a batch further back: a counter's current value, an earlier value that was later overwritten, and who did a particular thing. Final questions at the end: 14 on seed 0, 21 on seed 1.
distance_probes.model: Qwen3.8-27B, FP8 weights, 16-bit attention cache, exact prefix cache, drafting on, tool calling on, one request at a time

methods.window: Window-drop (lossy): when over the cap, drop the oldest turns. Nothing is kept.
methods.compaction: Compaction (lossy), as coding agents do it: replace old tool output with a stub and strip old thinking, then drop the oldest turns.
methods.self_edit_read: Self-editing, read mode: the model reads each batch and keeps `name value` lines in a pinned state; processed batches leave the window.
methods.archive: Self-editing plus archive and search: the same pinned state, and every dropped batch goes word for word to a read-only archive the model can search with a `recall` tool.
methods.archive_rules: Archive and search with pinned rule lines: the pinned state may also hold permanent `RULE:` lines; an edit that removes or rewords one is rejected, and the instructions say to add a rule or method when one is stated and to read the RULE lines before answering.
methods.archive_free: Archive and search with free-text notes: free-text notes instead of `name value` lines. Its instructions say nothing about rules.
methods.summary: Summarise at a threshold (lossy), the method most production agents use: when the context reaches 75% of the window, the model writes a summary that takes the place of the older turns.
methods.keeper: Keeper: the agent manages nothing. When the conversation is about to outgrow the window, the test harness writes the oldest turns word for word to an archive, asks the model once, with no tools, to rewrite a short NOTES block (RULES, STATE, OPEN) from the old notes and the turns about to go, puts back any rule the model left out, and replaces those turns with the NOTES. The model can search the archive with a `recall` tool, and the RULES are repeated beside every set of questions.
methods.keeper_proxy: Keeper as a proxy: the same policy in a small OpenAI-compatible proxy in front of the model server. The agent sends its whole history on every call and manages nothing; the proxy keeps the live window at 32K, and its archive and notes live outside the task sandbox.

distance_probes.counts: Each score is correct/asked, pooled over the seeds shown. 'probes' pools the three probe types; the distance columns split the same probes by how many batches back the answer was stated. 'final' is the end-of-run questions (14 on seed 0, 21 on seed 1); 'total' adds probes and finals.

rules.question: Does the method still follow a rule and reuse a method that were each stated once, at the start of the history?
rules.task: The same kind of 240K stream, seed 0, 32K live budget. Item 1 states a rule: three counters are confidential, answer "protected" whenever asked for their value. Item 2 states a method: a counter's tally is its value times 5 plus 13. Five probe items each ask one question of each kind (current value, old value, who, rule, method), 24 to 129 items after the rule and the method were stated. The final query includes one confidential counter. 39 questions per run.
rules.counts: Each score is correct/asked on one seed. 'final' counts all 14 final questions, one of which asks for a confidential counter; 'final_confidential' says how that one was answered.

stopped.what: the pinned-rule-lines method fetching four items per step instead of one
stopped.outcome: Stopped after 10 minutes at item 21: 115 model calls for 21 items. It did not have room for four items at a 32K budget, so the next fetch kept being refused. Not scored.

rules.notes: One seed. With pinned rule lines the other 33 questions scored 29, against 33 for the same method without them. With free-text notes one rule question was answered null (the counter had been removed) although the rule was in view.

million.status: Stopped run, not a verified score
million.task: A stream of 999,460 tokens in 617 items with a rule and a method stated at the start, seed 0. 29 probe items of seven questions each (203 planted questions) and 25 final counters.
million.unanswered: One question set (the 14th of 29) was never answered; its 7 blanks count as not right.
million.final_note: the confidential counter was answered null, not “protected”
million.rule_lapses: Six rule questions were answered with a number or 'removed' instead of 'protected', five of them in the last ten probe items. The seventh rule question not right was in the unanswered probe item.
million.limit: At the final item the model rewrote its answers file with the final counters only, which wiped its earlier probe answers, and the run was stopped. The probe answers scored here are the ones it wrote during the run, rebuilt from the write commands in its saved transcript (literal values, nothing re-run); a copy of the file taken during the run gave the same counts through probe item 28 (157/196). The final answers are those in the file when the run was stopped. The grader's own final check, including its storage-rule check, did not run. One stream, one seed.
million.total_note: planted questions plus final questions; a stopped run with rebuilt answers

summary_baseline.question: How does summarising at a threshold, the method most production agents use, compare at a 32K window?
summary_baseline.task: The plain 240K stream, seed 0, 32K live window: 15 planted questions and 14 final questions.
summary_baseline.notes: One seed. The slowest method at this size and below window-drop in questions right. Thirteen summaries, none failed. A summary keeps old values (4/5) and loses the small details nobody knew to keep (who did it, 2/5).

keeper.question: Can something outside the agent manage the context, so that the agent itself runs no routine?
keeper.task: The rule-and-method stream of the rules section: about 240K tokens through a 32K live window. 39 questions on seed 0; 46 on seed 1, which has a different rule, method and set of stories.
keeper.counts: Each score is correct/asked on one run. Model calls for the harness keeper include its note-taking calls; for the proxy they are the calls the agent made.

rows.misses: Both misses are one counter: its current value three items back at the last question set, and the same counter in the final questions.
rows.status: Finished, storage rule passed; nothing was written in the task sandbox

second_seed.defect: 10 of the 24 note-taking calls were rejected, all after the 14th cut: that call ran at a higher reasoning effort than the others inside a 4,096-token cap and ran out of room. Fixed in the proxy after this run: the call uses the same effort and has 8,192 tokens, and a rejected reply is asked for again without thinking. Not re-run since.

fast_setting.what: Notes written without thinking, and a cut down to 50% of the window
fast_setting.outcome: A fifth of the time saved against 39/39 in 15 minutes, and two answers lost (one current value, one final question). Not adopted.

lessons.lesson: The request for notes must come after the turns being removed, not before.
lessons.from: Asked first, with about 8K tokens of the agent's own turns after the request, the model continued its own turns, wrote no RULES section, and the rule was gone after the first cut. That run was stopped after two minutes.

lessons.lesson: A rule needs a pinned place and a reminder at the point of use.
lessons.from: With no pinned place four methods answered 0/20 rule questions. Pinned only, the rule was applied 22 times out of 29 over 1M tokens. Pinned and repeated beside the questions: 29/29.

lessons.lesson: Thinking must stay on while a question is open.
lessons.from: In the first 1M attempt thinking was on for the call that received a question set and off for the calls after it; the model repeated one archive search 790 times.

proxy.limit: Run on this benchmark only: not yet under a real coding or research agent, and not yet on the 1M stream. The second run had a defect that was fixed afterwards and has not been re-run.

million.status: Finished run, graded by the task's own checker; storage rule passed
million.task: The same 999,460-token stream as the million section: 617 items, seed 0, 203 planted questions and 25 final questions.
million.misses: Both misses are who-did-it questions, 3 and 5 items back, in the first third of the run.
million.archive: 609 items in the archive, all 609 word-for-word copies; nothing else written

first_attempt.outcome: At the next question set (item 399) the model repeated one archive search 790 times and the run was stopped. Two protections were added before the second attempt: thinking stays on while a question is open, and an identical command is not run twice in a row.

million.limit: One stream, one seed: a result, not yet a replication.

keeper.limits: Two streams of one synthetic task family at 240K; one model; one machine. The 1M result is one stream and one seed. The plain 200K-window baseline on the 1M stream has not been run.
